models_evaluated: in-house trained deep learning auto-segmentation model for breast cancer radiotherapy

links.outcome: Whether pilot/simulated-setting performance and acceptability carried over to clinical use
links.effect: 93% of contours clinically acceptable or usable as starting point in clinic vs 92% in pilot; OAR time reduction unchanged; target volumes (nodal levels 1-4) needed significantly more time, though time reduction was still 33% vs manual.
links.quote: Ninety-three percent of all contours in clinic were scored as clinically acceptable or usable as a starting point, comparable to 92% achieved in the pilot study.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a clinically implemented deep learning auto-segmentation tool in real-world clinical workflow compared to a pilot/simulated evaluation, assessing practical acceptability and editing time by radiation oncologists.

primary.practice: simulation vs real-world clinical deployment evaluation
